title: Bad Address
subtitle: memory fragment / misrouted refuge corridor
collapse_vector: Planetary refuge system routed to invalid territory

overview.summary: A residue object showing what happens when refuge systems keep confidently sending people to places that no longer exist.
overview.thesis: The map remained authoritative after the territory was gone.
overview.viewer_hint: Use this as the routing counterpart to administrative disappearance records.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.body: Address tables survived storm damage longer than the towns they described. That mismatch was enough for the system to keep exporting confidence after reality had already been redacted.

sections.title: Routing behavior
sections.body: Operators kept trusting cache warmth, checksum validity, and historical route success. The archive notes that each of those signals described the health of the map more than the health of the world.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.body: This file is readable because its residue is textual rather than acoustic, but its media state is still corrupted. The archive wants the operator to see the distinction between intact prose and intact transport.

events.label: Refuge routing rollout

events.label: Storm redaction
events.body: Whole territories are erased faster than address caches are invalidated.

events.label: Confidence export
events.body: Routing systems keep returning valid-looking destinations that no longer exist.

events.label: Corridor collapse
events.body: The refuge network becomes a machine for distributing false certainty.
